quote: The MWU distribution is ordered with respect to the strongest 'likelihood ratio' ordering as shown in the following theorem: Theorem (1) Let X ∼ MWU (α_1, λ_1) and Y ∼ MWU (α_2, λ_2), Then the following results hold true i) If α_1 < α_2 and λ_1 = λ_2 then X ≤_lr Y, X ≤_hr Y and X ≤_st Y ii) If α_1 = α_2 and λ_2 > λ_1 then X ≤_lr Y, X ≤_hr Y and X ≤_st Y
family: Modified weighted uniform MWU(α, λ): pdf f_WU(x) = λ(α + 1)(1 − λx)^α, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1/λ, α ≥ 0, λ ≥ 0 (eq. (6)); cdf F_WU(x) = 1 − (1 − λx)^{α+1} (eq. (7)); λ called the scale parameter and α the shape parameter
compared: shape α_1 < α_2 with common λ

hypotheses.text: Let X ∼ MWU (α_1, λ_1) and Y ∼ MWU (α_2, λ_2)
If α_1 < α_2 and λ_1 = λ_2
likelihood ratio order (X ≤_lr Y) if f_X(x)/f_Y(x) decreases in x
hypotheses.formal: X ≤_lr Y iff f_X/f_Y decreasing on the support

conclusion.direction: X ≤_lr Y, i.e. MWU(α_1, λ) ≤_lr MWU(α_2, λ) for α_1 < α_2

quantifiers: all α_1 < α_2 (α ≥ 0), all λ ≥ 0 common; x ∈ [0, 1/λ) (proof: 'increasing if x < 1/λ')
ambiguity: λ = 0 is allowed by 'λ ≥ 0' but makes the pdf degenerate. The definitions in Section 3.6 (i)–(iii) do not mention supports.

hazard rate order (X ≤_hr Y) if h_X(x) ≥ h_Y(x) for all x
